description: Refresh package-lock.json on its own schedule. A refresh is only true of the tree it resolved against, so every merge to main leaves this branch describing a package.json that has moved; rebasing on the base branch regenerates it, keeping its green check a statement about the merge someone is actually about to make.
No age gate on the refresh itself: npm resolves the transitive versions here, and it is the only side that sees them.

packageRules.description: A major needs a proper read of its changelog, which rarely happens the week it lands. Park it on the dashboard so it stops holding a concurrency slot, and tick it there when someone is ready to do that work.
A lock file refresh carries no update anyone is waiting on, so it takes a concurrency slot only when a real update does not need it.
Manage github-actions SHA pins manually; a digest-bump PR would run CI with the new SHA before anyone reviews it.
Batch non-major updates into one PR to keep the weekend run quiet.

A 0.x release makes no compatibility promise, so a minor or a patch there can break like a major does. Each gets its own PR rather than riding in a batch, where one broken member holds up the safe ones.
connect and connect-node are one release line, and both are built on @bufbuild/protobuf, so they move together.

typescript and @typescript/native are pinned to deliberately chosen preview builds (npm aliases of the TS 6/7 previews); do not auto-PR them, surface them on the dashboard so a bump is a conscious choice. tsup and vitest batch with the other non-major updates.
